witnessRunPrefixNote: witnessRunPrefixes are the first 8 characters of the private recording run ids replayed for the case; the original 2026-10-05 recordings are 14802609 and a8ed1cce.
method: Per-case adjudication of the 122 frozen cases (18 conditions) against the final strict release binary. Every witness is a LOCAL strict replay of genuine production recordings on that binary; raw physical differences are retained in the private run outputs. A row status is the case verdict for each declared transport. Rules are owner decision ledger entries; 1391 and 1401 are coordinator readings recorded in the ledger. What is compared on REST rows: original r1/r2 rows: status and normalized body (no headers or wire length were recorded). H1 and A: status, normalized body and recorded bodyBytes equality. B: status and the semantic body; physical layout is kept as a debt, not compared. C: status and semantic body for the case verdict; bodyBytes and bodySha256 equality is the retained physical verdict. D: ok/code/status and the normalized body with timestamp evidence; for REST the physical check is only that the local body size and digest are well formed and within the caps and that the replay clock is bound, so REST body bytes are not compared (D compares raw bytes only for recovered native Pull responses). No comparison judges any response header. The original-row comparator sorts topics, subscriptions and snapshots list members before comparing (a base comparator rule, not an owner relation). Basis text names private evidence files of the per-case proof.

statuses.MATCH: every witness MATCH, no rule needed
statuses.MATCH_BY_RELATION: MATCH once the listed rules are applied exactly
statuses.EXCLUDED_STEP: the listed rules exclude named steps; every other step MATCH or MATCH_BY_RELATION

rules.651: Transport mapping: path-body-mismatch over native gRPC is observed as routing metadata versus message resource name (2026-09-30).
rules.897: Strict accepts a connection without an Authorization header as the PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST exception (registered divergence); a configured credential that fails local verification answers the recorded 401/UNAUTHENTICATED shape (2026-10-05).
rules.1100: Generated acknowledgement ids are compared by type, presence, wire tag, non-emptiness, message correspondence and actual ACK behaviour, not by value or internal length; clockStart is a replay parameter bound to each recording (2026-10-08).
rules.1135: message.publishTime of a proven publication is compared by relation (generated seconds/nanos and the encoding widths they imply), not by value (2026-10-09).
rules.1146: LIST order and page boundaries across separate runs are not compared; each environment proves the complete set through its own cursors. Snapshot.expireTime is compared by relation (2026-10-09).
rules.1171: StreamingPull S06 (ordering disabled, no key): receipt frame position and order are not compared; each receipt maps to one successful publication and its ACK (2026-10-09).
rules.1193: Dead-letter forwarded messages: sink publishTime compared by relation (2026-10-10).
rules.1194: Dead-letter forwarded messages: CloudPubSubDeadLetterSourceTopicPublishTime equals each environment's own source publishTime (2026-10-10).
rules.1199: Dead-letter R5/N5: deliveryAttempt after the recorded inactivity boundary restarts at 1 or previous+1 and then advances by exactly 1 (2026-10-10).
rules.1203: Named unfiltered positive-control windows permit per-Pull partition and receipt-order differences; valid-Seek windows permit an eligible marker in a different Pull inside the original window (2026-10-10).
rules.1204: C R9: relative interleaving across different ordering keys permitted; same-key order and ACK barriers retained (2026-10-10).
rules.1209: C N7 (run 567e1cd860a1): empty-string map value presence or omission and the ancestor lengths it implies (2026-10-10).
rules.1213: C R8/N8: Pull partition and cross-key receipt order inside the finite window permitted; same-key order and ACK gating retained (2026-10-10).
rules.1215: C N9 (one response of run 45298b949da0): cross-key placement order inside one Pull permitted (2026-10-10).
rules.1243: Snapshot 14/4: adaptive comparison (count 2, attempts 3, own latest ACK, separate post-ACK Pull returns 0, 20 s per Pull) in both recordings and transports; raw differences retained; final-binary qualification required (2026-10-11).
rules.1319: Snapshot N13: bounded post-Seek comparison (Seek window at most 90 s, equivalent sequential constructions, successful current-delivery ACK before the next Seek); only early empty responses and delivery timing may differ (2026-10-11).
rules.1383: The production REST GET 404 right after create in /conditions/3/cases/0 and /conditions/14/cases/2 is excluded from comparison; fireemu returns the steady-state 200 (2026-10-11; description corrected by 1385).
rules.1385: Production REST negative cache for subscriptions and snapshots (about 9.5 s after a slow 404, reproduced in some orders, counterexamples exist, rule not established) is NOT emulated; the affected GET steps of /conditions/3/cases/0, /conditions/14/cases/2 and /conditions/1/cases/4 R2 are excluded; strict unchanged; follow-up after the release (2026-10-11).
rules.1390: Original 2026-10-05 recordings (r1/r2) stored only REST status and body: no response headers and no wire length. As clarified by 1404, their REST rows MATCH when status and body content are equal; headers were neither recorded nor compared (2026-10-12).
rules.1391: The /conditions/1/cases/4 R2 exclusion covers the GET right after CREATE and the same-name cleanup GET (2026-10-12, coordinator reading of 1385).
rules.1392: Original ordering cells (/conditions/11/cases/0, 1, 4): the key production serves next on later Pulls varies by run and transport; per-key order, no keyed/unkeyed mixing in one Pull and the cell delivered set must match (2026-10-12).
rules.1394: Differences explained only by (1) delivery order of messages without an ordering guarantee and (2) a Pull returning fewer messages than available (including 0) MATCH when the cell delivered set, each message content and, with ordering enabled, per-key order match; cases /conditions/6/cases/4, 6/8, 9/0, 9/4, 11/2, 14/3; fireemu answers immediately and does not simulate empty Pulls (2026-10-12).
rules.1395: Original ordering cells are replayed with identity acknowledgements (the replay acknowledges its own delivery of the message production acknowledged) on the final binary (2026-10-12).
rules.1399: Original ordering cells in the second recording: MATCH when on both sides each key delivered set is a prefix of its publish order, keyed and unkeyed are never mixed in a Pull, and the whole-cell difference is only the tail of a key held by an unacknowledged delivery at cell end (2026-10-12).
rules.1400: Clarifies 1399: MATCH when each side holds at most one ordering key by an unacknowledged delivery at cell end and the whole-cell difference is only the tails of those held keys; per-key prefix, per-key order and no unkeyed/keyed mixing still required; any unsuccessful Pull or Acknowledge on the ordered subscription on either side is DIVERGES (2026-10-12).
rules.1401: Coordinator interpretation of 1400: a side holds an ordering key when it delivered fewer of the key messages than the other side and its last delivery of the key is unacknowledged at cell end; keys whose final batch is unacknowledged on both sides with equal counts are not held (2026-10-12).
rules.1402: Clarifies 1394 for a Pull limited by maxMessages: the set condition reads each delivered message is one of the cell published messages with equal content, its id correlates with the same-side publish reply, and the delivered counts are equal; which member a limited Pull returns is non-guarantee (1) of 1394; raw differences stay in the record (2026-10-12).
rules.1404: Clarifies 1390 for the original REST rows: equal status and equal body content; the record says plainly that headers were neither recorded nor compared, and discloses the Content-Type difference found in header-bearing captures (production application/json; charset=UTF-8, fireemu application/json), fixed separately in v0.17; the closure evidence stays bound to the release binary (2026-10-12).
